This disables Toc's window scroll tracking. ```tsx ``` ## When to use - Component reference pages with installation, usage, and API sections. - Long guides whose sections need direct links. - Articles with nested headings and a reading position indicator. ## When not to use - Page hierarchy: use Breadcrumb. - Navigation between different pages: use Sidebar or Navigation Menu. - Switching panels that hide other content: use Tabs. ## API | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `items` | `readonly TocEntry[]` | required | Entries in document order; empty arrays render nothing. | | `label` | `string` | `"On this page"` | Visible title and accessible navigation label. | | `activeId` | `string` | automatic | Controlled current heading id; disables automatic tracking. | | `scrollOffset` | `number` | `96` | Pixels below the viewport top for automatic tracking. | | `className` | `string` | – | Merged last. | | native nav props | `ComponentProps<"nav">` | – | Includes ref, style, aria attributes, and event handlers. | `TocEntry` has `id: string`, `title: string`, and optional `depth: 2 | 3` (default `2`). Slots are `toc`, `toc-title`, `toc-track`, `toc-rail`, `toc-indicator`, `toc-list`, `toc-item`, and `toc-link`. ## Motion contract One persistent indicator follows the active entry. Its top and bottom edges use the shared physics spring, then render as translation and vertical scale on a one-pixel base. Wrapped labels determine the destination's length. Edges stay inside the rail, and interrupted movement preserves velocity. Text and `aria-current` follow the current section immediately. Activating a link smoothly scrolls the actual scrolling host to its heading in full mode. The destination respects the heading's scroll margin and the host's scroll padding; movement stays within the host's scroll bounds. | Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Active section or label size changes | Indicator translateY / scaleY | `layout.shared` / `spring.morph` | Yes; the existing indicator follows the latest target. | | Section link activation | Native scroll offset | `scroll.navigate` / `duration.page` / `ease.inOut` | Yes; another link retargets from the current position. | | Initial measurement / restored selection | Instant placement, no entrance | — | — | | reduced | Instant indicator placement and section navigation | — | Stops springs; completes an active navigation before paint. | | none | Instant placement and navigation, no animation clock | — | Stops springs; completes an active navigation before paint. | Zero provider timeScale also places the indicator immediately. Restoring full motion keeps the settled position until the next section or size change. A ResizeObserver supplies geometry; no layout is read during render. Navigation uses one token-backed tween, with no separate CSS/native smooth-scroll clock. Wheel, touch, pointer input, scrolling keys, resizing, history traversal and external hash changes cancel it at the current position. Positive clock changes retime the current trip; reduced/none or zero clock complete it immediately. No interrupted trip restarts later. The site's mobile disclosure stays instant. Initial hashes, reload, history traversal and no-JS links keep native behavior; only an explicit unmodified section link activation starts the recipe. ## Accessibility - A labelled `nav` contains an ordered list of native links. - Tab and Shift+Tab move between links; Enter activates the same navigation as a primary click. - The active link has `aria-current="location"` and a stronger text weight. The decorative indicator is hidden from assistive technology. - Heading targets need matching, unique ids. Offset their scroll margin to account for sticky headers. - Native anchors remain usable before hydration and without JavaScript. Automatic tracking requires JavaScript. - Navigation preserves unrelated URL parameters and history state, pushes the new fragment and notifies hashchange listeners. Back/forward use native scroll restoration. - Completion focuses the heading without scrolling a second time. A temporary `tabindex="-1"` is removed on blur/unmount; caller-supplied tabindex is preserved. Interrupted navigation never steals focus. - Modified/new-tab clicks and caller-cancelled clicks retain native behavior. ## Keyboard interactions | Keys | Action | | --- | --- | | Tab / Shift+Tab | Move between native section links. | | Enter | Scroll to the focused link's heading, update the fragment and focus the heading on completion. | | Scrolling keys / Tab / Escape | Interrupt an ongoing smooth navigation. | The indicator never receives focus or replaces a link when its destination changes. ## Responsiveness and performance The component fills its parent and wraps long labels. The caller owns placement, sticky position, height limits, and overflow. For documentation layouts, place it in a sticky right column with an independently scrollable list. Smaller viewports can use a native disclosure near the title; a floating disclosure list avoids moving the article when opened. Automatic tracking uses passive window scroll events, resize events, and a ResizeObserver, with cleanup on unmount. It reads heading positions in those callbacks, updates state only when the active id changes, and selects the final heading at the page bottom. It tracks headings present when mounted; remount after dynamically replacing the document or pass new items. The server renders the first entry as current; hydration corrects it for a deep link or restored scroll position. Before measurement, a static border marks the current link, including without JavaScript. The first measured position is immediate. The indicator remains mounted through selection and mode changes. The indicator's two edge values animate; the list's layout does not interpolate. Section navigation measures its destination once on activation, then writes native offsets without per-frame layout reads. A ResizeObserver tracks wrapped labels, font changes, and a mobile disclosure becoming visible. Motion and the shared Cadence provider/runtime are installed dependencies; a provider is optional and system reduced motion is respected standalone. The T3 source budget is 12 KB gzip; dependency and page budgets are measured separately. ## Notes for AI - Build the list from the same heading tree that renders the article so links and ids cannot drift. - Use this Cadence original for document navigation; it has no pinned shadcn counterpart. - Do not use a component instance to generate heading ids or to own application routing.
